title: Ignoring Tests and Compiler Lints
goal: Control test execution with ignore attributes and lint control attributes.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Compiler Lints

sections.text: Not all tests should run on every `cargo test` invocation. Heavy or slow tests can be marked with `#[ignore]`.

sections.caption: #[ignore] skips the test unless cargo test is run with -- --ignored.

sections.text: The Rust compiler and Clippy provide lints to detect potential bugs and style issues. You can configure lints using attributes.
Use `#[allow(lint_name)]` to suppress a specific warning, or `#[deny(lint_name)]` to turn a warning into a hard build error.

sections.caption: #[deny] turns a warning into a hard compile error if the lint triggers.

sections.text: Attributes can be attached to individual functions, blocks, or modules to control lints locally.

explanation: Control test execution with ignore attributes and lint control attributes.
